title: Distributed real-time SlowDoS attacks detection over encrypted traffic using Artificial Intelligence
venue: Journal of Network and Computer Applications

value.name: Generated SlowDoS datasets (High-connections, Medium-connections, Low-connections)
value.quote: Three datasets have been generated using a different amount of clients and concurrent connections: High-connections, Medium-connections, Low-connections.

datasets_evaluated.evidence: Three datasets have been generated using a different amount of clients and concurrent connections: High-connections, Medium-connections, Low-connections.

label_source.evidence: In order to gather genuine real-time data, we have implemented a traffic generator leveraging JMeter for normal HTTPs traffic and slow-http-test to launch the different SlowDoS attacks.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: the features include statistical time-related information of the stream of packets set up between a client and a web server

value: Duration in microseconds; Number of packets sent in 1 s in uplink and downlink; Number of bytes sent in 1 s in uplink and downlink; Maximal, minimal and average packet size in uplink and downlink; Maximal, minimal and average size of TCP window in uplink and downlink; Maximal, Minimal and average time-to-live in uplink and downlink; Percentage of packets with different TCP flags in uplink and downlink; Percentage of packets with different properties in uplink and downlink; Number of new connections to the same destination host; Percentage of new connections from the current host; Total number of active connections to the same destination host; Percentage of active connections from the current host
features_used.evidence: Duration in microseconds, (4) Number of packets sent in 1 s in uplink and downlink, (5) Number of bytes sent in 1 s in uplink and downlink, (6) Maximal, minimal and average packet size in uplink and downlink

feature_groups.evidence: the features include statistical time-related information of the stream of packets set up between a client and a web server

model_family.value: Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM); Autoencoder (Deep Learning); sGMM
model_family.evidence: our AI model called sGMM, that combines GMM and DL, is compared with the state of the art...our AI-based attack detector uses an Auto-Encoder (AE), which is a neural network

split_protocols.evidence: For this purpose, a 10-fold validation was performed using the 25% of randomly chosen test data, respecting a balance between normal and anomalous communications.

main_split.evidence: a 10-fold validation was performed using the 25% of randomly chosen test data

metrics.evidence: The metrics used to evaluate the quality of the attack detection models were both, Receiver Operating Characteristics (ROC) curve and Area Under the Curve (AUC).

granularity.evidence: network packets are processed into conversation and sent to the ML layer

first_n_packets.evidence: the average time required for detecting is 9.8 s with a deviation of +-2.4 s in some tests. This time includes every stage of our application: network monitoring, conversation processing and machine learning classification.

cost_reported.evidence: the average time required for detecting is 9.8 s with a deviation of +-2.4 s in some tests. This time includes every stage of our application: network monitoring, conversation processing and machine learning classification.

hardware.value: VM CPUs at 2.1 GHz, 8 GB to 16 GB RAM, 8 to 16 cores
hardware.evidence: Streaming Processor: 2 machines. 8 GB memory and 16 cores each. It includes layer (2) and (3). Every virtual machine CPU is running at 2.1 GHz and have a network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.
